shortDescription: Poland's manufacturing sector contracted for a 16th straight month in August as output and new orders fell faster and supply-chain pressures intensified amid the Iran war, a business survey showed on Tuesday.

children: Poland's manufacturing sector contracted for a 16th straight month in August as output and new orders fell faster and supply-chain pressures intensified amid the Iran war, a business survey showed on Tuesday.
The S&P Global Poland Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.3 in August from 49.0 in July, sliding further below the 50 mark that separates growth from contraction.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 49.6.
Suppliers' delivery times lengthened for a 16th successive month, to the greatest degree since June 2022, despite a further reduction in purchasing activity.

New orders fell for a 17th consecutive month, with firms citing weak demand, a slowdown in sectors such as construction and import competition from mainland China. Export orders also declined for a ninth month, though only modestly.
Production dropped at a steeper rate in August and has fallen 14 times in the past 16 months.
Manufacturers also cut headcounts, reversing July's increase, although the pace of job shedding was weaker than in the first half of 2026.
Input price inflation accelerated for the first time in four months. Factory gate prices rose at the slowest pace in the current six-month run of increases, suggesting pressure on margins.
